audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2, 3 and 4-5 were all labelled 'Skill' even though every why line on those rows describes Sylas bullying a Nautilus who cannot leave, and the 2+ item row read 'Skill' against its own Sylas-flavoured why.
audit.why: The packet chart and the already-audited mirror nautilus__sylas both read Skill / Sylas / Sylas / Sylas / Nautilus / Sylas / Sylas. Nautilus takes level 6 because Depth Charge is point-click and fires through Sylas's engage; the rest of the lane belongs to the champion with the burst-heal and two charges of mobility.
audit.corrected: All five disagreeing rows flipped in matched phases[].side + win[] pairs, ratings moved with them, and phases[4].why rewritten so the level 6 row no longer claims the swing goes to Sylas.

audit.why: Four spikes present and right: Sylas's level 2-3 kit completion, Nautilus's level 6 Depth Charge, Riftmaker, and Nautilus's late initiator role. Only the phase ratings disagreed with them.
audit.corrected: Ratings realigned; spike text left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields describe Abduct as a stun ('E2 stuns him in place', 'Q slow sets up E2 stuns', 'cancel your E2 stun', 'no stun'), and wants.foe[2] tells the reader he cannot stun.
audit.why: Riot's text for Abscond's recast says only that Sylas throws his chains and pulls himself to an enemy he hits; the derived kit carries no hardCC flag on E. The mirror audit reached the same conclusion and also declined to assert a stun. What actually matters here is the opposite: the recast drags Sylas INTO Nautilus's passive root and Riptide, and Depth Charge (120/100/80s, point-click, 825 range) knocks him up regardless.
audit.corrected: Every stun claim replaced with the chain-pull description; the real threat — his point-click R landing through the engage — stated instead.

audit.why: Dredge Line's 14/13/12/11/10s cooldown is already the stated metronome and the early text quotes 14s correctly at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Added Abscond's own 13/12/11/10/9s downtime to wants.foe[2] so the reader knows which of his own cooldowns is the punishable one.

edits.before: Hijack online — you now own a copy of Nautilus's ultimate. The all-in math and every 2v2 swing your way.
edits.after: Depth Charge is point-click and unmissable — he fires it into your engage and Hijack cannot stop his own cast.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Engaging with both E charges spent — Abduct only pulls you in, and a melee mage has no exit without it.

edits.before: Engaging with both E charges spent — no shield, no stun, and you're a melee mage standing in the open.
edits.after: Abduct chains you to him, not the other way round — that is anchor-root and Riptide range for free.

edits.before: Full kit: E1 shield eats his passive auto on approach, E2 stuns him in place, Q slow lands for free, W heals back the exchange — he has no answer.
edits.after: Full kit: E1 closes the gap, E2 chains you onto him, the Q slow lands free and W heals the exchange back — with no dash he cannot leave it.

edits.before: Reach Iceborn Gauntlet and force all-ins on E cooldown when you can't stun or shield
edits.after: Force the all-in during Abscond's 9-13s downtime, when you have no way to leave

edits.before: The levels 4-5 window is pure farm bullying — your Q slow sets up E2 stuns, Conqueror stacks fast in extended trades, and W on a tanky Nautilus returns a genuinely alarming amount of HP. Keep Dredge Line's timer in your head: the moment it fires and misses, that's your green light to E2 in and go. At 6 caution is warranted — Depth Charge is point-click and instant-cast, and Nautilus can fire it INTO your engage to cancel your E2 stun with a knockup that interrupts everything. He may also have his jungler waiting. Take the E2-W-Q trade, don't immediately commit to an all-in at 6, and decide whether to Hijack his R for later teamfight use or save it for an immediate 2v2 with your jungler.
edits.after: The levels 4-5 window is pure farm bullying — your Q slow keeps him in Abduct range, Conqueror stacks fast in extended trades, and W on a tanky Nautilus returns a genuinely alarming amount of HP. Keep Dredge Line's 14-10s timer in your head: the moment it fires and misses, that's your green light to chain in and go. At 6 caution is warranted — Depth Charge is point-click at 825 range, and Nautilus can fire it INTO your engage, knocking you up out of the rotation you already spent. He may also have his jungler waiting. Take the E2-W-Q trade, don't commit to an all-in at 6, and decide whether to Hijack his R for later teamfight use or for an immediate 2v2.

notes: The Abduct stun correction is Medium confidence, matching the mirror: it rests on Riot's ability text and the absence of a hardCC flag on E, not on a wiki read. One League Wiki check on Abduct would settle it for the whole champion, since the same boilerplate stun claim appears in every sylas matchup file I have audited.
